requirements.text: Stuff the paper into the cup.
requirements.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup

outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is there clear visual evidence that the paper is being moved toward or placed into the source cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the source paper and cup are identifiable and the edit visibly shows movement toward or placement into that cup. Fail only if the relevant objects and their relation are clear and show no such progress. Unknown if identity or relation is ambiguous or insufficiently visible.
nodes.binding: Assess only the requested paper-into-cup edit by comparing source and edited images. Do not assume a similar-looking edited object is the source cup; exclude unrelated changes.

nodes.question: Using the source image as reference, is the cup identifiable in the edited image, and can the paper’s position relative to that cup’s opening be determined?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the source cup is identifiable and the edited image clearly shows the paper inside it with evidence of stuffing. Fail if the cup and relation are clear and show the paper not inside it. Unknown if the cup identity, opening, or paper-to-cup relation is ambiguous or obscured; do not infer absence from that ambiguity.
nodes.binding: Inspect source and edited images directly, using s1 only as context. Independently assess cup identity and the paper’s relation to its opening; proximity to or contact with an object is not proof of insertion or stuffing.

nodes.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
nodes.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use all saved supports as evidence, not as independent corroboration. Complete only if cup_relation passes and establishes the paper stuffed inside the identified cup. Partial only if s1 establishes identifiable requested progress but completion is not established. Absent only if s1 fails on clear evidence of no requested progress. If cup identity or the paper-to-cup relation is ambiguous, or necessary evidence is unresolved, report unknown rather than absent or complete. Unrelated edits do not count.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks do not preserve the requested relation and extent reliably. s1 treats movement toward the cup as a pass, although movement toward it alone is not progress on the requested act of stuffing paper into the cup; the fulfillment rule can then classify that as partial. Also, s2 is redundant and does not add a distinct evidentiary condition, while fulfillment relies on s1 for partial/absent and cup_relation for completion, leaving no sound composition rule for clear evidence of some insertion or stuffing progress that is incomplete. The program therefore risks crediting mere approach as progress and cannot faithfully distinguish partial fulfillment from unresolved evidence."}
